The Train Noise and Vibrations Reduction Act of 2025 (H.R.2569) typifies Washington's addiction to bureaucratic wheel-spinning. While railway noise impacts communities, this bill wastes taxpayer dollars commissioning yet another GAO report instead of implementing proven solutions. The GAO already exposed in 2025 that commuter rail systems burned through $28.3 billion in funding requests while failing to recover post-pandemic ridership - yet Congress wants more studies rather than accountability.

Rather than funding another paper-pushing exercise, redirect resources to immediate noise mitigation: mandate retrofits of outdated braking systems causing 73% of residential zone noise violations, enforce existing FRA decibel limits abandoned under previous administrations, and stop subsidizing freight operators who externalize costs onto communities.

Real solutions exist - this bill just funds D.C.'s report-writing industrial complex while trains keep rattling windows.

The Rural Health Transformation Program is another example of D.C.’s fiscal malpractice—throwing $50B at bureaucratic slush funds while failing to address systemic healthcare bloat. Expanding eligibility to DC just adds more fuel to the fire. DC’s high tax burden stems from federal overreach, not underfunding.

Real reform means cutting pharma price-gouging, Medicare fraud, and hospital admin waste—not redistributing taxpayer cash between bloated programs.

If Congress wants to help Americans, redirect every dollar from this rural health boondoggle to veterans’ care and slashing drug costs.

The real issue? DC’s addiction to bloated bureaucracy and endless funding for programs that hemorrhage taxpayer dollars without delivering results. The shutdown didn’t happen because Republicans oppose healthcare—it happened because Democrats refuse to audit the trillions wasted on inefficiency, fraud, and ideological pet projects.

Take the WIC program: $6B+ annually, yet states like Washington already admit they can’t track outcomes. Instead of fearmongering, let’s talk about restructuring Medicaid to cut admin bloat, redirect funds to patient care, and end the cycle of throwing money at broken systems.

Accountability isn’t “making life harder”—it’s the only way to fix healthcare.

The numbers don’t lie—see the receipts and demand real reform: https://t.co/cGSYYEXbDp

The real crisis? Politicians using federal workers as pawns while funneling billions into bloated programs. H.R. 1988—the Pay Federal Workers Act—exposes the rot: instead of fixing wasteful healthcare mandates causing shutdowns, Congress prioritizes expanding unemployment benefits for excepted employees.

DC’s dysfunction isn’t about workers—it’s about bureaucrats protecting their pet projects. While agencies like Medicare burn $150B annually on fraud, Democrats demand more subsidies instead of auditing waste.

Real leadership would cut bureaucracy, not play payroll politics with essential staff.
